Drawing From a Penalty Read as a Prior

Source: R/penalty_draw.R
penalty_draw.Rd

Returns a draw from the distribution whose negative log-density is the penalty, at the given hyperparameters, with NA in the coordinates that the distribution does not determine.

Usage

penalty_draw(pen, theta, ...)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same, as for the other generics of the package.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

A numeric vector of length pen@n_coef, NA in the coordinates that the prior does not determine and possibly NA throughout.

Details

A proper penalty is a negative log-prior, and penalty_value() includes its normalizing constant for that reason. Simulating from a model that contains a random effect, a ridge or a lasso therefore amounts to drawing those coefficients from this distribution.

Branches that draw

A separable penalty draws from its own parent family, so a Gaussian prior gives Gaussian effects, a Laplace prior gives Laplace effects and a Student t prior gives heavy-tailed effects. A univariate parent is drawn once per coordinate, and a multivariate parent once per block of coordinates.

A quadratic, additive or structured penalty is a Gaussian prior with precision \(S(\theta)\), and two cases are drawn directly. Where \(S\) is diagonal each coordinate is drawn on its own with standard deviation \(S_{jj}^{-1/2}\), which covers a ridge and a smooth in a basis whose penalty is diagonal (such as the Demmler-Reinsch basis); a zero on that diagonal is a direction that the prior does not determine, and its entry is NA. Where \(S\) is not diagonal but has full rank, one Cholesky factor \(S = R^\top R\) gives the draw, since \(\beta = R^{-1}z\) has covariance \(S^{-1}\).

A rank-deficient \(S\) that is not diagonal, such as the penalty of an anisotropic tensor smooth, gives a vector of NA. The prior is flat along the null space of \(S\), and a draw restricted to the range would require a basis of that range, a decomposition that these branches do not compute.

SCAD and MCP are improper and are not densities, so their draws are NA everywhere. A branch that is not quadratic and does not register a method of its own also gives NA everywhere.

The map

A separable penalty is a prior on \(D\beta\), so a draw of the coefficients inverts the map. Without a map the draw is returned as it is. Under a diagonal map, such as the one that standardization produces, each coordinate is divided by its diagonal entry, and a coordinate whose entry is zero is not determined by the prior and is NA. Under any other map, including a square invertible one, the draw is not inverted and every coordinate is NA. A quadratic penalty does not need this step, because penalty_matrix() returns the precision in the coefficients themselves.

Undetermined coordinates

The coordinates that the prior does not determine are NA rather than zero. A caller that draws a whole model has its own rule for a coefficient that is not covered by any prior; an intercept is the ordinary case. A zero would be indistinguishable from a prior that concentrates at zero, so it would not show which coordinates remain to be filled.

Methods

The method on the base class penalty() draws from a quadratic penalty (for which is_quadratic() is TRUE) read as a Gaussian prior, as described above, and returns NA for any other branch. A separable penalty registers penalty_draw.DistribPenalty().

See also

penalty_value() for the negative log-density from which the draw is made, is_proper() for whether the penalty is a proper prior, penalty_matrix() for the precision of the Gaussian branches.

Examples

set.seed(1)

# A Gaussian prior on ten effects gives ten Gaussian draws.
ridge <- ridge_penalty(n_coef = 10)
round(penalty_draw(ridge, list(lambda = 4)), 3)
#>  [1] -0.313  0.092 -0.418  0.798  0.165 -0.410  0.244  0.369  0.288 -0.153

# The scale is that of the prior, so a larger lambda shrinks the draw.
c(loose = stats::sd(penalty_draw(ridge, list(lambda = 0.25))),
  tight = stats::sd(penalty_draw(ridge, list(lambda = 100))))
#>      loose      tight 
#> 2.13902967 0.09556076 

# The lasso is a Laplace prior and gives Laplace draws.
round(penalty_draw(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 6), list(lambda = 2)), 3)
#> [1]  0.874 -0.266 -0.043 -0.204  0.180 -0.331

# The unpenalized direction of a smooth is NA.
P <- diag(c(0, rep(1, 4)))
penalty_draw(quadratic_penalty(P), list(lambda = 1))
#> [1]          NA -0.05380504 -1.37705956 -0.41499456 -0.39428995

# A diagonal map with a zero entry leaves that coordinate NA.
penalty_draw(lasso_penalty(map = Matrix::Diagonal(x = c(1, 0, 2))),
             list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] -0.04845261          NA  0.65222622

# SCAD is not a density, so every coordinate is NA.
penalty_draw(scad_penalty(n_coef = 3), list(lambda = 1, a = 3.7))
#> [1] NA NA NA
